import numpy as np

# Data for FY 1953 to FY 1962 (Gold as independent variable X, Silver as dependent variable Y)
# From Treasury Bulletin tables (monetary stocks of gold and silver)
years = [1953, 1954, 1955, 1956, 1957, 1958, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1962]
gold = np.array([22462.8, 21927.0, 21677.6, 21799.1, 22622.9, 21356.2, 19704.6, 19322.2, 17550.2, 16435.2])
silver = np.array([3814.3, 3863.1, 3922.4, 3994.5, 4116.6, 4306.0, 4414.1, 4394.5, 4346.5, 4317.4])

# Calculate linear regression: silver = a + b*gold
# Using numpy polyfit (degree 1)
b, a = np.polyfit(gold, silver, 1)

# Calculate R-squared
y_pred = a + b * gold
ss_res = np.sum((silver - y_pred) ** 2)
ss_tot = np.sum((silver - np.mean(silver)) ** 2)
r_squared = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

print(f"Linear Regression: Silver = {a:.6f} + {b:.6f} * Gold")
print(f"R-squared: {r_squared:.6f}")
print(f"R-squared (rounded to 2 decimals): {round(r_squared, 2)}")

# Also print data for verification
for i, year in enumerate(years):
    print(f"FY {year}: Gold = {gold[i]}, Silver = {silver[i]}")
